diagnostic_steps.action: Parse log stream for CPU throttling events
findings: CPU throttling active on api-frontend pods (45% of CPU time throttled)
Backend experiencing CPU starvation and database timeouts
Container CPU usage at 950m against 1000m limit
Throttled periods: 13500 out of 30000 total periods
Node CPU idle time at 8% (near capacity)
Root cause: CPU limits too low for actual workload demand
Contributing factor: No horizontal scaling to distribute load
CPU request/limit ratio not optimized for burst workloads
Node capacity insufficient for current workload
diagnostic_steps.root_cause: CPU limits too restrictive combined with lack of horizontal scaling

recommendations.command: kubectl set resources deployment api-frontend --limits=cpu=2000m --requests=cpu=1000m -n api-service
recommendations.rationale: Double CPU limit to 2000m with 1000m request for better burst handling

recommendations.command: kubectl set resources deployment api-backend --limits=cpu=4000m --requests=cpu=2000m -n api-service
recommendations.rationale: Increase backend CPU limits to prevent starvation
Enable HPA to scale horizontally at 60% CPU utilization
Enable HPA for backend to handle increased load

recommendations.command:
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: high-priority-api
value: 1000
globalDefault: false
description: "High priority for API services"
EOF
recommendations.rationale: Create priority class to ensure API pods are not evicted

recommendations.command:
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: api-frontend-pdb
  namespace: api-service
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-frontend
EOF
recommendations.rationale: Ensure minimum replicas during scaling events

remediation_validation: Monitor CPU throttling rate (should drop below 10%)
Verify p95 latency returns to baseline (< 300ms)
